Origin Access Control (OAC) replaces OAI for S3 origins; origin failover via origin groups; Origin Shield adds a central cache layer
Signed URLs/cookies for private content; field-level encryption; mutual TLS to origins (Jan 2026)
CloudFront Functions: JavaScript, <1 ms, viewer request/response only; Lambda@Edge: Node/Python, up to 30 s (origin) and network access
Flat-rate plans (Nov 2025): Free $0, Pro $15, Business $200, Premium $1,000/month bundling CDN, WAF, DDoS, Route 53 DNS and logs with no overages
services.pricingModel: Pay-as-you-go per GB out (by geography) and per 10k requests, with free tier (1 TB/month), or flat-rate monthly plans with usage allowances; Lambda@Edge/Functions billed separately; no charge for origin fetch from AWS origins.

comparesWith.difference: Global Accelerator gives static anycast IPs and routes TCP/UDP over the AWS backbone without caching; CloudFront caches HTTP content.
S3 can host static websites directly but only over HTTP in one Region; CloudFront adds HTTPS, caching and global edge.

recentLaunches.title: Flat-rate pricing plans with no overages (Free/Pro/Business/Premium)
Mutual TLS support for origins

interviewTips: Maximize cache hit ratio: minimize forwarded headers/cookies/query strings, use versioned object names instead of invalidations
Lock down origins so users cannot bypass CloudFront (OAC for S3, custom header/prefix list for ALB)

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.oneLiner: Highly available DNS (100% SLA), domain registration, health checks, routing policies, Resolver for hybrid DNS and the new Global Resolver.
whenToUse: Public and private hosted zones; alias records to AWS resources at the zone apex
Traffic management: failover, latency, weighted, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue, IP-based routing
Hybrid DNS with Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints and DNS Firewall
whenNotToUse: Sub-second failover requirements (DNS TTL caching delays failover — consider Global Accelerator)
keyFacts: 100% availability SLA for DNS query answering
Alias records are free to query, can point to apex, and target ELB, CloudFront, S3 websites, API Gateway, VPC endpoints, etc.
Health checks from multiple global locations; calculated health checks; CloudWatch alarm-based checks for private resources
Application Recovery Controller provides routing controls for highly reliable manual failover
Accelerated recovery (Nov 2025): public hosted zone control-plane changes available within 60 min RTO if us-east-1 is impaired (replica in us-west-2), no extra cost
Route 53 Global Resolver (GA Mar 2026): internet-reachable anycast DNS resolver across 30 Regions
services.pricingModel: Per hosted zone per month, per million queries (alias queries to AWS resources free), health checks per month, Resolver endpoints per ENI-hour and queries, domain registration per year.

comparesWith.difference: Global Accelerator fails over in seconds using anycast IPs without relying on DNS TTLs; Route 53 is DNS-based.
CloudFront routes requests to origins at the edge; Route 53 resolves names to endpoints.

recentLaunches.title: Accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records (60-minute RTO)
Route 53 Global Resolver generally available
Palo Alto Networks Advanced DNS Security on Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall

interviewTips: Know the Route 53 control plane is in us-east-1 while the data plane is global — design failover on data-plane features (health checks, ARC routing controls)
Choose routing policy from requirement (latency vs geolocation compliance vs weighted canary)

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.oneLiner: Managed load balancers: Application (L7 HTTP/gRPC), Network (L4 TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC) and Gateway (L3 appliance insertion).
whenToUse: ALB for HTTP/HTTPS routing by host/path/header, OIDC/Cognito auth, JWT verification, WebSockets, gRPC, Lambda targets
NLB for extreme performance, static IPs/Elastic IPs per AZ, TLS passthrough, PrivateLink services, QUIC passthrough
GWLB for transparent insertion of third-party firewalls/IDS using GENEVE
whenNotToUse: Global anycast entry points (Global Accelerator) or CDN caching (CloudFront)
keyFacts: ALB: target types instance, IP, Lambda; weighted target groups for blue/green; slow start; idle timeout default 60 s
NLB: preserves client IP, millions of requests per second, ultra-low latency, one static IP per AZ; supports security groups
Cross-zone load balancing: on by default for ALB (free), off by default for NLB/GWLB (cross-AZ data charges)
Deregistration delay (connection draining) default 300 s
ALB client-credential JWT verification for M2M (Nov 2025); NLB QUIC passthrough (Nov 2025)
services.pricingModel: Per LB-hour plus Load Balancer Capacity Units (LCU for ALB, NLCU for NLB, GLCU for GWLB) based on new connections, active connections, processed bytes and rule evaluations.

comparesWith.difference: API Gateway adds API keys, usage plans, request validation, caching and per-request pricing; ALB is cheaper at high volume for simple HTTP routing.
Global Accelerator fronts Regional ELBs with static anycast IPs for multi-Region failover.

recentLaunches.title: NLB supports QUIC protocol in passthrough mode
ALB client credential flow with JWT verification

interviewTips: Pick ALB vs NLB vs GWLB from protocol and requirements (static IP, client IP preservation, PrivateLink)
Explain health checks, sticky sessions trade-offs and TLS termination/re-encryption with ACM

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.oneLiner: Managed front door for REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs with auth, throttling, caching, usage plans and now response streaming.
whenToUse: Serverless APIs fronting Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB and other AWS services (service integrations)
Partner/public APIs requiring API keys, usage plans, request validation, WAF and custom domains
Private APIs reachable only through interface VPC endpoints
whenNotToUse: Very high sustained request volumes where per-request pricing exceeds ALB cost
Long-running synchronous requests beyond the integration timeout (use async patterns)
keyFacts: Account throttle default 10,000 RPS with 5,000 burst per Region (lower in some newer Regions), adjustable
Integration timeout 50 ms–29 s by default; REST Regional/private APIs can request a higher timeout (at the cost of throttle quota)
Payload size 10 MB (REST/HTTP); WebSocket frames 32 KB, messages 128 KB, connections up to 2 hours, 10-minute idle timeout
REST vs HTTP APIs: HTTP APIs are cheaper/faster with JWT authorizers; REST adds usage plans, caching, request validation, WAF, private endpoints, response streaming
Authorizers: IAM (SigV4), Cognito user pools, Lambda authorizers, JWT (HTTP APIs); mutual TLS on custom domains
Response streaming for REST APIs (Nov 2025) and developer portal capabilities
services.pricingModel: REST: per million requests (tiered) plus optional cache per hour; HTTP: lower per-million price; WebSocket: per million messages plus connection-minutes; plus data transfer.

comparesWith.difference: ALB is priced per hour/LCU and lacks API management features; API Gateway is per request with auth/throttling built in.
AppSync is managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions; API Gateway serves REST/HTTP/WebSocket.

recentLaunches.title: Response streaming for REST APIs, developer portal capabilities and new TLS security policies

interviewTips: Know the 29-second default integration timeout and the async pattern (202 + polling/WebSocket/callback) for long jobs
Throttling layers: account → stage/method → usage plan per API key; protect Lambda concurrency accordingly

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.oneLiner: Dedicated private network connections from on-premises to AWS at 1, 10, 100 or 400 Gbps (dedicated) or 50 Mbps–25 Gbps (hosted).
whenToUse: Consistent latency/bandwidth and lower data-transfer-out rates for hybrid workloads
Large ongoing data movement, regulated connectivity, or private access to many VPCs via Direct Connect gateway + TGW
whenNotToUse: Quick or temporary connectivity (Site-to-Site VPN is up in minutes; DX takes weeks)
Encrypted-by-default requirements without MACsec or VPN overlay
keyFacts: Virtual interfaces: private VIF (VPC via VGW/DXGW), transit VIF (TGW via DXGW), public VIF (AWS public endpoints)
Dedicated connections 1/10/100/400 Gbps; hosted connections via partners 50 Mbps–25 Gbps; LAG up to 4 connections (max 2 at 100/400 Gbps)
Not encrypted by default: use MACsec (10/100/400 Gbps at select locations) or IPsec VPN over DX
Resiliency: maximum resiliency = 2 locations × 2 connections; SLA depends on model; BGP failover testable with Fault Injection Service (Dec 2025)
Direct Connect gateway is global: associate up to 6 TGWs per DXGW
services.pricingModel: Port-hours by speed (dedicated) or partner pricing (hosted), plus data transfer out at reduced DX rates; data in is free.

comparesWith.difference: VPN is encrypted over the internet, fast to set up, up to 1.25 Gbps (or 5 Gbps large) per tunnel; DX is private, consistent and higher bandwidth.
TGW is the Regional hub; DX (transit VIF + DXGW) is the on-prem link into it.

recentLaunches.title: Test Direct Connect BGP failover with AWS Fault Injection Service
AWS Interconnect GA — managed multicloud and last-mile private connectivity

interviewTips: Always design a backup path: second DX at another location, or VPN over internet as a cheaper backup
Explain BGP path preference (local preference communities, AS_PATH prepend, longest prefix) for active/passive

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.oneLiner: Regional network hub that connects thousands of VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect with transitive routing and segmentation via route tables.
whenToUse: Hub-and-spoke networking across many VPCs and accounts (share with AWS RAM)
Centralized egress/inspection VPC (with appliance mode) and shared services
Inter-Region connectivity via TGW peering
whenNotToUse: Just two or three VPCs with no transitive needs (VPC peering is cheaper — no per-GB processing)
Global multi-Region WAN with policy-driven segmentation (Cloud WAN is simpler at scale)
keyFacts: Up to 5,000 attachments per TGW; 5 TGWs per account per Region (adjustable); 20 route tables per TGW (adjustable); 10,000 total routes
Bandwidth up to 100 Gbps per VPC attachment per AZ (each direction) and up to 7.5 million pps
MTU 8,500 bytes for VPC/DX/peering traffic; 1,500 for VPN
VPN attachments support ECMP to aggregate tunnels (dynamic routing only)
Peering attachments are static-routed; up to 50 peering attachments per TGW
Appliance mode keeps flows symmetric through stateful inspection appliances
services.pricingModel: Per attachment-hour plus per GB of data processed.

comparesWith.difference: Cloud WAN is a global managed WAN with a central policy document and automatic segment attachment; TGW is Regional and configured per route table.
VPC Lattice handles service-to-service (L7) connectivity including overlapping CIDRs; TGW handles IP routing.
VPC peering is point-to-point and non-transitive with no data processing fee.

interviewTips: Design segmentation with multiple TGW route tables (prod, non-prod, shared, inspection) and propagation/association
Remember the per-GB processing cost when comparing to peering for heavy east-west traffic

services.name: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
services.oneLiner: Managed IPsec VPN with two tunnels per connection between on-prem gateways and a VGW, Transit Gateway or Cloud WAN.
whenToUse: Fast, encrypted hybrid connectivity or as a backup to Direct Connect
Branch offices connecting to a TGW; encrypting traffic over DX (private IP VPN)
whenNotToUse: Guaranteed bandwidth/latency needs (Direct Connect)
Individual remote users (AWS Client VPN)
keyFacts: Each connection has 2 tunnels in different AZs; standard tunnels up to 1.25 Gbps, Large Bandwidth tunnels up to 5 Gbps (Nov 2025, TGW/Cloud WAN only, not VGW)
ECMP across tunnels on TGW for higher aggregate throughput (dynamic BGP routing required)
Accelerated VPN uses Global Accelerator edge locations (TGW attachments)
Static or BGP routing; IKEv1/IKEv2; tunnel bandwidth can be modified on existing connections (May 2026)
services.pricingModel: Per VPN connection-hour plus data transfer out; accelerated VPN adds Global Accelerator charges.

comparesWith.difference: DX is private and consistent but slower to provision; VPN is encrypted over the internet and quick to set up.

recentLaunches.title: 5 Gbps Large Bandwidth tunnels
Modify tunnel bandwidth on existing VPN connections

interviewTips: Explain how to exceed per-tunnel limits with ECMP on TGW and why VGW cannot do that

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.oneLiner: Private, unidirectional connectivity to AWS services, SaaS and your own services via interface VPC endpoints — no IGW, NAT or peering.
whenToUse: Exposing a service (behind NLB) to many consumer VPCs/accounts with overlapping CIDRs
Private access to AWS APIs (e.g. SSM, ECR, Secrets Manager, Bedrock) from isolated subnets
Consuming SaaS from AWS Marketplace privately
whenNotToUse: Bidirectional or full network connectivity between VPCs (use TGW/peering)
keyFacts: Interface endpoint = ENIs in your subnets with private DNS; endpoint policies restrict actions/resources
Endpoint services are fronted by NLB (or GWLB for Gateway Load Balancer endpoints)
Works across accounts and with overlapping IP ranges; cross-Region PrivateLink is supported for endpoint services
VPC resource endpoints / service networks (via VPC Lattice) extend access to resources such as databases
services.pricingModel: Per interface endpoint per AZ-hour plus per GB processed; gateway endpoints (S3/DynamoDB) are free.

comparesWith.difference: Lattice is an application-layer service network with auth policies and many-to-many connectivity; PrivateLink is one service per endpoint.
TGW provides full IP routing between networks; PrivateLink exposes a single service one-way.

recentLaunches.title: Bedrock PrivateLink support for OpenAI-compatible (bedrock-mantle) endpoints in 14 Regions

interviewTips: Use PrivateLink when the requirement is "expose one service to many customers with overlapping CIDRs"

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.oneLiner: Two static anycast IPs that route TCP/UDP traffic over the AWS global network to optimal Regional endpoints with fast failover.
whenToUse: Multi-Region active-active/active-passive apps needing failover in seconds without DNS caching issues
Non-HTTP workloads (gaming, VoIP, IoT) or clients that need fixed IP allow-listing
whenNotToUse: Cacheable HTTP content (CloudFront is cheaper and caches)
keyFacts: Standard accelerators route to NLB, ALB, EC2, Elastic IP endpoints; custom routing accelerators map to specific EC2 instances/ports
Traffic dials and endpoint weights control per-Region traffic share; health checks fail over in ~30 s or less
Client affinity option (source IP) for stateful apps; BYOIP supported
services.pricingModel: Fixed hourly fee per accelerator plus Data Transfer-Premium per GB depending on source/destination Regions.

comparesWith.difference: CloudFront caches at edge for HTTP(S); Global Accelerator proxies TCP/UDP without caching.
Route 53 failover depends on DNS TTLs; Global Accelerator failover is at the network layer with static IPs.

interviewTips: Mention GA when the interviewer says "static IPs", "non-HTTP", or "fast Regional failover"

services.name: Amazon VPC Lattice
services.oneLiner: Application networking service that connects, secures and monitors service-to-service communication across VPCs and accounts.
whenToUse: Microservices across many accounts/VPCs (EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda targets) with IAM-based auth policies
Overlapping CIDRs or teams that should not manage network routing
Sharing resources such as databases across accounts via resource configurations
whenNotToUse: Bulk network-level connectivity (e.g. on-prem to VPC routing) — use TGW/Cloud WAN
Very high-throughput data-plane traffic where per-GB processing cost dominates
keyFacts: Constructs: service network, service, listener (HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC/TLS/TCP), target group, auth policy
Auth policies use IAM SigV4 for zero-trust service-to-service authorization
Shared across accounts using AWS RAM; integrates with ECS Service Connect and EKS Gateway API controller
services.pricingModel: Per service-hour, per GB processed and per million requests; resource configurations billed per hour/GB.

comparesWith.difference: PrivateLink exposes a single service via endpoints; Lattice builds a many-to-many service network with L7 routing and auth.
TGW routes IP networks; Lattice routes application requests irrespective of IP overlap.

interviewTips: Position Lattice for platform teams wanting app-level connectivity and IAM auth without a service mesh sidecar

services.name: AWS Cloud WAN
services.oneLiner: Managed global wide-area network built from a central JSON policy, with segments, core network edges per Region and automatic attachment.
whenToUse: Global enterprises connecting many Regions, branches (SD-WAN), data centers and VPCs with consistent segmentation
Replacing multiple peered Transit Gateways with policy-driven routing
Private multicloud links via AWS Interconnect associated with Cloud WAN
whenNotToUse: Single-Region hub-and-spoke (TGW is sufficient and cheaper)
keyFacts: Core network policy defines segments, Regions (core network edges), attachment policies (tag-based) and segment sharing
Service insertion steers traffic through inspection (network function groups)
Can peer with existing Transit Gateways for migration; supports VPN (incl. 5 Gbps tunnels) and Connect (GRE/BGP) attachments
services.pricingModel: Per core network edge-hour, per attachment-hour, and per GB data processing.

comparesWith.difference: TGW is Regional with manual inter-Region peering; Cloud WAN is global with centralized policy.
DX provides the physical on-prem link; Cloud WAN orchestrates the global network over which traffic routes.

recentLaunches.title: AWS Interconnect – multicloud GA (Google Cloud first; associate with Cloud WAN)
AWS Interconnect multicloud with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure GA

interviewTips: Explain segments as the equivalent of TGW route tables but global and policy-defined

services.name: AWS Network Firewall
services.oneLiner: Managed, stateful network firewall and IPS (Suricata-compatible rules) deployed per AZ in VPCs or attached to Transit Gateway.
whenToUse: Centralized egress/east-west inspection with domain allow-lists, IPS signatures and TLS inspection
Compliance requirements for deep packet inspection inside AWS
whenNotToUse: L7 HTTP attack protection for web apps (use WAF)
Simple port/IP filtering already met by security groups/NACLs
keyFacts: Stateless and stateful rule groups; Suricata rule syntax; AWS managed threat signature rule groups
Firewall endpoints deployed per AZ; route traffic via route tables or native TGW attachment
TLS inspection decrypts/re-encrypts with ACM certificates
Central management across accounts with AWS Firewall Manager
services.pricingModel: Per firewall endpoint-hour plus per GB processed; Feb 2026 price reductions include NAT gateway discounts and removal of TLS inspection charges.

comparesWith.difference: WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests at CloudFront/ALB/API Gateway; Network Firewall inspects all VPC traffic at L3–L7.
Shield protects against DDoS; Network Firewall enforces traffic policy and IPS.

recentLaunches.title: Price reductions: NAT gateway discounts and removal of TLS inspection charges

interviewTips: Draw the centralized inspection VPC with TGW appliance mode for symmetric routing

services.name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
services.oneLiner: Global service for authenticating principals and authorizing every AWS API call with identity-, resource-, boundary-, session- and org-level policies.
whenToUse: Roles for workloads (EC2 instance profiles, Lambda execution roles, EKS Pod Identity) instead of long-term keys
Cross-account access via role assumption and resource policies; federation from external IdPs (SAML/OIDC)
Guardrails with permissions boundaries plus Organizations SCPs/RCPs
whenNotToUse: Workforce SSO across many accounts — use IAM Identity Center rather than IAM users
End-user (customer) identities for apps — use Cognito
keyFacts: Evaluation: explicit Deny > SCP/RCP allow required > resource policy > identity policy > permissions boundary > session policy; default implicit deny
Managed policy max 6,144 characters; inline role policies 10,240 characters aggregate; up to 10 (adjustable to 20) managed policies per role
Default quotas: 5,000 IAM users and 1,000 roles per account (roles adjustable); role session duration up to 12 h (1 h max when role chaining)
IAM Access Analyzer: external/unused access findings, policy validation and policy generation from CloudTrail
Outbound identity federation (Nov 2025) lets workloads get short-lived JWTs for external services without stored secrets
IAM is eventually consistent — changes can take seconds to propagate
services.pricingModel: No charge for IAM; Access Analyzer unused-access and custom policy checks are billed per resource/check.

comparesWith.difference: Identity Center centralizes workforce SSO and permission sets across accounts; IAM defines the underlying roles/policies per account.
Cognito handles customer/app user sign-up and sign-in; IAM authorizes AWS API calls.
SCPs/RCPs in Organizations set the maximum permissions; IAM policies grant within those limits.

recentLaunches.title: IAM outbound identity federation for accessing external services
IAM Policy Autopilot — open-source MCP server that generates policies from code
AWS IAM Role Manager automatically sets up service roles

interviewTips: Walk through the policy evaluation logic for a cross-account request (both identity and resource policy must allow)
Least privilege in practice: start broad in dev, then refine with Access Analyzer policy generation and last-accessed data
Use condition keys: aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:RequestedRegion, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, tags for ABAC

services.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
services.oneLiner: Workforce single sign-on and centralized access to multiple AWS accounts and applications, federated with your IdP.
whenToUse: Multi-account organizations granting humans access via permission sets
Connecting Okta/Entra ID/Google via SAML + SCIM provisioning; trusted identity propagation to analytics services
whenNotToUse: Machine/workload identities (use IAM roles)
Customer-facing app users (use Cognito)
keyFacts: One Identity Center organization instance in the management account (delegated admin possible); account instances for standalone apps
Permission sets are provisioned as IAM roles in each assigned account
Identity sources: Identity Center directory, Active Directory, or external IdP
Multi-Region support extended to the Identity Center directory for DR (Jul 2026)
services.pricingModel: No additional charge.

comparesWith.difference: IAM users/roles are per account; Identity Center centrally manages human access across accounts.
Cognito serves app end-users; Identity Center serves employees/workforce.

recentLaunches.title: Multi-Region support extends to Identity Center directory

interviewTips: Recommend Identity Center + permission sets + SCIM instead of IAM users for any multi-account landing zone

services.name: AWS Organizations
services.oneLiner: Central management of multiple AWS accounts with OUs, consolidated billing and authorization policies (SCPs, RCPs) plus management policies.
whenToUse: Multi-account strategies separating workloads, environments and security/log archive accounts
Preventive guardrails via Service Control Policies and Resource Control Policies
Tag, backup, AI opt-out and declarative policies across accounts
whenNotToUse: Single-account setups with no need for isolation (but most production customers should use multiple accounts)
keyFacts: SCPs limit maximum permissions of principals in member accounts; they never grant and do not affect the management account
RCPs (Nov 2024) cap permissions on resources (e.g. S3, KMS, STS, SQS, Secrets Manager) regardless of caller
Default quota 10 accounts (increase on request); OU nesting up to 5 levels; SCP max size 5,120 characters; up to 5 SCPs attached per entity
Consolidated billing aggregates usage for volume tiers and shares RIs/Savings Plans (can be restricted)
Delegated administrator accounts for security services (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, etc.)
services.pricingModel: No charge.

comparesWith.difference: Control Tower automates a best-practice landing zone on top of Organizations with managed controls and Account Factory.
IAM grants permissions in an account; SCPs/RCPs restrict what can ever be granted.

recentLaunches.title: AWS Billing Transfer — centrally manage billing across multiple organizations

interviewTips: Sketch an OU structure (Security, Infrastructure, Workloads/Prod/NonProd, Sandbox, Suspended) and sample SCPs (deny leaving org, region deny, protect CloudTrail)

services.name: AWS Control Tower
services.oneLiner: Sets up and governs a secure multi-account landing zone with managed preventive, detective and proactive controls and Account Factory.
whenToUse: Greenfield or brownfield landing zones that need best-practice structure quickly
Standardized account vending (Account Factory, AFT for Terraform) with baselines
whenNotToUse: Organizations with highly customized existing landing zones where Control Tower opinions conflict (use Organizations + custom IaC, or LZA)
keyFacts: Creates Security OU with Log Archive and Audit accounts; centralized CloudTrail and Config
Controls: preventive (SCPs/RCPs), detective (Config rules), proactive (CloudFormation hooks); Control Catalog includes Security Hub controls (176 added Dec 2025)
Drift detection alerts when resources deviate from the landing zone
Dedicated controls experience (Nov 2025) lets you use controls without a full landing zone
services.pricingModel: No charge for Control Tower; you pay for underlying services (Config, CloudTrail, S3, Security Hub, etc.).

comparesWith.difference: Organizations is the underlying account/policy service; Control Tower is the opinionated orchestration layer.
Account Factory uses Service Catalog products to vend accounts.

recentLaunches.title: Controls-dedicated experience in Control Tower
176 additional Security Hub controls in the Control Catalog

interviewTips: Know preventive vs detective vs proactive controls and give an example of each

services.name: AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
services.oneLiner: Managed creation and control of encryption keys in FIPS 140-3 validated HSMs, integrated with most AWS services via envelope encryption.
whenToUse: Encryption at rest for S3, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB etc. with customer managed keys for control, rotation and auditing
Signing/verification (RSA, ECC, EdDSA) and HMAC; multi-Region keys for cross-Region encrypted replication
whenNotToUse: Single-tenant HSM with full key custody (use CloudHSM or KMS custom key store / external key store)
Encrypting large payloads directly — KMS Encrypt handles up to 4 KB; use data keys (envelope encryption)
keyFacts: Key types: AWS owned, AWS managed (aws/service), customer managed (CMK); symmetric AES-256 by default
Direct Encrypt/Decrypt limit 4 KB; GenerateDataKey for envelope encryption
Automatic rotation for customer managed keys yearly by default (configurable 90–2,560 days); on-demand rotation
Key policies are the primary access control (plus grants and IAM); deletion has a 7–30 day waiting period
Shared request quotas per account per Region (e.g. 5,500–100,000 cryptographic RPS depending on Region); S3 Bucket Keys reduce calls
Multi-Region keys share key material and ID across Regions
services.pricingModel: $1 per customer managed key per month (plus rotations), per 10,000 API requests; AWS managed keys have no monthly fee.

comparesWith.difference: Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets (encrypted with KMS); KMS manages keys, not secrets.
ACM issues and manages TLS certificates; KMS manages encryption/signing keys.

recentLaunches.title: Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA) support

interviewTips: Explain envelope encryption and why it scales; cross-account key usage needs both key policy and IAM permission
Watch for KMS throttling with SSE-KMS at high S3 request rates (use S3 Bucket Keys)

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.oneLiner: Stores, retrieves and automatically rotates secrets such as database credentials and API keys, encrypted with KMS.
whenToUse: Database credentials with managed rotation (RDS, Aurora, Redshift, DocumentDB)
Cross-Region replicated secrets for DR; fine-grained access with resource policies
whenNotToUse: Plain configuration values or high-volume, non-secret parameters (SSM Parameter Store standard tier is free)
keyFacts: Max secret size 64 KB; versions tracked with staging labels (AWSCURRENT, AWSPENDING, AWSPREVIOUS)
Rotation via Lambda functions or managed rotation; schedules down to every 4 hours
Secret replication to other Regions; caching clients and the Secrets Manager Agent reduce API calls (pre-fetch and role assumption added May 2026)
Post-quantum hybrid TLS (ML-KEM) for API calls (Apr 2026)
services.pricingModel: Per secret per month (replicas billed as secrets) plus per 10,000 API calls.

comparesWith.difference: Parameter Store offers free standard parameters and SecureString but no built-in rotation; Secrets Manager rotates and replicates.
KMS manages keys; Secrets Manager manages secret values encrypted by those keys.

recentLaunches.title: Post-quantum TLS with hybrid ML-KEM key exchange
Secrets Manager Agent adds pre-fetching and IAM role assumption

interviewTips: Compare Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store on rotation, cost and size limits (Parameter Store advanced: 8 KB)

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.oneLiner: Customer identity and access management: user pools for sign-up/sign-in (OIDC/OAuth 2.0) and identity pools for temporary AWS credentials.
whenToUse: Web/mobile app authentication with hosted Managed Login, MFA, social and SAML/OIDC federation
Issuing JWTs for API Gateway/ALB authorization; machine-to-machine client credentials
Identity pools to give app users scoped AWS credentials (e.g. upload to S3)
whenNotToUse: Workforce SSO to AWS accounts (IAM Identity Center)
keyFacts: User pool feature tiers: Lite, Essentials (default), Plus (threat protection)
Tokens: ID, access (default 1 h, 5 min–1 day) and refresh (default 30 days, up to 10 years)
Lambda triggers customize flows (pre sign-up, pre token generation, custom auth challenges)
Multi-Region replication of user pools (Jun 2026); password-hash import via CSV (Jul 2026)
Cognito Sync is closed to new customers (Jul 30, 2026) — use AppSync/DynamoDB instead
services.pricingModel: Per monthly active user (MAU) by feature tier, with a free tier for Lite/Essentials; M2M billed per app client and token requests; identity pools free.

comparesWith.difference: Identity Center is for employees accessing AWS; Cognito is for customers accessing your app.
IAM authorizes AWS API calls; Cognito identity pools exchange app tokens for IAM role credentials.

recentLaunches.title: Identity pools support AWS PrivateLink
Multi-Region replication for user pools
Password hash import in CSV user import

interviewTips: Distinguish user pools (authentication, JWTs) from identity pools (AWS credentials)

services.name: AWS WAF
services.oneLiner: Web application firewall for CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access with managed and custom rules.
whenToUse: Blocking OWASP Top 10 patterns (SQLi, XSS), bad IPs, geo restrictions and rate-based abuse
Bot Control, account takeover/fraud prevention (ATP/ACFP) and CAPTCHA/challenge actions
whenNotToUse: Network-layer (L3/L4) inspection inside a VPC (use Network Firewall)
keyFacts: Web ACL capacity default 1,500 WCUs (up to 5,000 with additional cost)
Rule actions: Allow, Block, Count, CAPTCHA, Challenge; rate-based rules with custom aggregation keys
Managed rule groups from AWS (Core rule set, Known bad inputs, IP reputation) and Marketplace vendors
Request body inspection default 8 KB for ALB/AppSync (16 KB default for CloudFront/API Gateway, configurable up to 64 KB)
Centrally deployed across accounts with Firewall Manager
services.pricingModel: Per web ACL per month, per rule per month, per million requests; extra for Bot Control, Fraud Control and additional WCUs; included in CloudFront flat-rate plans.

comparesWith.difference: Shield mitigates DDoS; WAF filters application-layer requests (and is used by Shield Advanced for L7 mitigation).
Network Firewall inspects VPC traffic at L3–L7; WAF inspects HTTP requests at supported edges/LBs.

interviewTips: Start managed rules in Count mode, then tune; combine rate-based rules with CloudFront for DDoS absorption

services.name: AWS Shield
services.oneLiner: DDoS protection: Shield Standard is automatic and free for all customers; Shield Advanced adds L7 mitigation, SRT support and cost protection.
whenToUse: Business-critical internet-facing apps needing 24/7 Shield Response Team and DDoS cost protection (Advanced)
Protecting CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator, ELB and Elastic IPs
whenNotToUse: Low-risk workloads where Shield Standard plus CloudFront/WAF best practices suffice
keyFacts: Shield Standard: automatic L3/L4 protection at no cost
Shield Advanced: $3,000/month per organization with a 1-year commitment plus data transfer out fees; includes WAF for protected resources
Automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation creates WAF rules; health-based detection with Route 53 health checks
Cost protection credits for scaling charges caused by DDoS
services.pricingModel: Standard free; Advanced monthly subscription (1-year term) plus usage-based data transfer fees.

comparesWith.difference: WAF filters requests by rules; Shield detects and mitigates volumetric and protocol attacks.

interviewTips: DDoS-resilient reference: Route 53 + CloudFront + WAF + Shield Advanced in front of ALB/ASG, minimizing attack surface

services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
services.oneLiner: Managed threat detection using ML and threat intel on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and runtime/S3/EKS/RDS/Lambda/malware signals.
whenToUse: Continuous detection of compromised credentials, crypto-mining, exfiltration and malicious IPs across all accounts
Runtime monitoring for EKS, ECS/Fargate and EC2; malware scanning for EBS and S3 uploads
whenNotToUse: Preventive controls (GuardDuty detects; pair with SCPs, Security Hub automation)
keyFacts: Enable org-wide via delegated administrator; no agents for foundational sources (agents for runtime monitoring)
Extended Threat Detection correlates multi-stage attack sequences (EKS, and EC2/ECS added Dec 2025)
Findings to EventBridge and Security Hub for automated response
AI-powered investigations (preview, Jun 2026) automate threat analysis with confidence scoring
services.pricingModel: Per GB/events analyzed for each data source (CloudTrail events, Flow/DNS logs GB, S3 events, runtime vCPU-hours, malware scan GB); 30-day free trial.

comparesWith.difference: Detective helps investigate root cause of findings; GuardDuty generates the findings.
Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings from GuardDuty and others.
Inspector finds vulnerabilities (CVEs, reachability); GuardDuty finds active threats.

recentLaunches.title: Extended Threat Detection for Amazon EC2 and Amazon ECS
AI-powered investigations (preview)

interviewTips: Describe an automated response: GuardDuty finding → EventBridge → Lambda/SSM to isolate instance, revoke sessions

services.name: AWS Security Hub
services.oneLiner: Unified cloud security operations: correlates GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and Security Hub CSPM findings into prioritized exposures in near real time.
whenToUse: Single pane of glass for security findings and posture across an organization
CSPM compliance checks against CIS, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, PCI DSS, NIST (Security Hub CSPM)
Automated ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow) and response workflows
whenNotToUse: Deep investigation of individual incidents (use Detective / Security Lake + SIEM)
keyFacts: Re-launched GA Dec 2, 2025 with near real-time risk analytics, exposure correlation and 1-year trends; previous product renamed Security Hub CSPM
Findings use the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) in the new Security Hub; CSPM uses ASFF
Cross-Region aggregation and delegated administrator for the organization
Security Hub Extended (2026) adds curated partner solutions; network reachability scanning (Jul 2026); Azure resource monitoring (Jun 2026)
services.pricingModel: Resource-based pricing that consolidates charges across integrated security services; Security Hub CSPM billed per security check and finding ingestion.

comparesWith.difference: GuardDuty produces threat findings; Security Hub correlates and prioritizes across sources.
AWS Config records resource configuration and evaluates rules; Security Hub CSPM uses Config to run controls.
Security Lake stores normalized raw security logs long-term; Security Hub manages findings.

recentLaunches.title: New AWS Security Hub GA with near real-time analytics and risk prioritization
Security Hub Extended — curated partner security solutions
Monitoring for Microsoft Azure resources
Network Scanning identifies internet-reachable resources

interviewTips: Show currency: "Security Hub" now means the unified exposure/risk product; the controls engine is Security Hub CSPM

services.name: Amazon Inspector
services.oneLiner: Automated, continuous vulnerability management for EC2, ECR container images, Lambda functions and code repositories.
whenToUse: Continuous CVE and network reachability scanning without scheduling scans
Shift-left scanning of images in CI/CD and code security scanning
whenNotToUse: Runtime threat detection (GuardDuty) or data classification (Macie)
keyFacts: Uses SSM Agent for EC2 (or agentless snapshot-based scanning); ECR enhanced scanning; Lambda standard and code scanning
Inspector risk score adjusts CVSS with network reachability and exploitability
SBOM export (CycloneDX/SPDX); Inspector Classic reached end of support
services.pricingModel: Per EC2 instance scanned per month, per container image scanned (initial and rescans), per Lambda function per month.

comparesWith.difference: GuardDuty detects active threats; Inspector finds vulnerabilities to patch.
SSM Patch Manager remediates; Inspector identifies what needs patching.

interviewTips: Pair Inspector findings with SSM Patch Manager and Security Hub automation for closed-loop remediation

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.oneLiner: Discovers and classifies sensitive data (PII, credentials, financial data) in S3 using ML and pattern matching, and flags bucket security risks.
whenToUse: Data privacy programs (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI) needing inventory of where sensitive data lives in S3
Detecting publicly accessible or unencrypted buckets
whenNotToUse: Sensitive data in databases or file systems outside S3 (not scanned natively)
keyFacts: Automated sensitive data discovery samples objects across the estate; targeted discovery jobs for full scans
Managed data identifiers plus custom identifiers (regex + keywords) and allow lists
Findings to EventBridge and Security Hub; org-wide via delegated admin
services.pricingModel: Per bucket evaluated per month, per object monitored for automated discovery, and per GB inspected for discovery jobs.

comparesWith.difference: GuardDuty S3 Protection detects suspicious access; Macie finds what sensitive data exists.

interviewTips: Mention Macie for "where is our PII" questions and pair it with S3 Block Public Access and KMS

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.oneLiner: Records AWS API activity (management, data and network activity events) for audit, security analysis and compliance.
whenToUse: Organization trails delivering all accounts' events to a central, locked-down S3 bucket
Investigating who did what, when and from where; triggering EventBridge rules on API calls
whenNotToUse: Application logs or OS logs (CloudWatch Logs)
New CloudTrail Lake deployments — Lake stopped accepting new customers on May 31, 2026
keyFacts: Event history: 90 days of management events free per Region
Trails: first copy of management events free; data events (S3 object-level, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB items) billed
Log file integrity validation with SHA-256 digests; SSE-KMS encryption; delivery typically within ~5 minutes
CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API call rates/error rates
CloudTrail Lake: closed to new customers May 31, 2026; use CloudWatch unified data store or Security Lake/Athena
services.pricingModel: Per 100,000 data/extra management events delivered, Insights per 100,000 events analyzed; S3 storage separate; Lake ingestion/retention for existing customers.

comparesWith.difference: Config records resource configuration state over time; CloudTrail records API calls.
CloudWatch handles metrics/logs/alarms; CloudTrail can send events to CloudWatch Logs for alerting.

recentLaunches.title: CloudTrail Lake moves to maintenance (no new customers from May 31, 2026)

interviewTips: Protect the trail: org trail, dedicated log archive account, S3 Object Lock, SCP denying StopLogging/DeleteTrail

services.name: AWS Config
services.oneLiner: Continuously records resource configurations and relationships and evaluates them against managed/custom rules and conformance packs.
whenToUse: Compliance auditing and configuration history ("what did this security group look like last Tuesday?")
Detective controls with auto-remediation via SSM Automation
Org-wide aggregators for inventory across accounts and Regions
whenNotToUse: Preventing changes before they happen (use SCPs, CloudFormation Hooks, proactive controls)
keyFacts: Recording: continuous or periodic (daily); configuration items stored in S3; timeline for 7 years retention by default
Rules: managed (hundreds), custom Lambda or Guard (policy-as-code); triggered on change or periodically
Conformance packs bundle rules and remediation; aggregator gives multi-account multi-Region view
Expanded resource type coverage (e.g. 30 new types incl. EKS and Amazon Q in Feb 2026)
services.pricingModel: Per configuration item recorded (continuous vs periodic rates), per rule evaluation, per conformance pack evaluation.

comparesWith.difference: CloudTrail answers who made the API call; Config answers what the resource state was and whether it complied.
Security Hub CSPM uses Config-based controls and aggregates their findings.

recentLaunches.title: New resource types across EC2, SageMaker and S3 Tables
30 new resource types including EKS, Amazon Q and IoT

interviewTips: Control Config cost by recording only needed resource types or periodic recording in non-prod

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
services.oneLiner: Provisions and auto-renews public and private TLS certificates for integrated services, now with exportable public certs and ACME support.
whenToUse: Free public TLS certificates for CloudFront, ALB/NLB, API Gateway, App Runner and more with automatic renewal
Private certificates from AWS Private CA for internal mTLS
Automating public certificate issuance for non-integrated endpoints via ACME (Jun 2026)
whenNotToUse: Extended Validation (EV) certificates (not offered)
keyFacts: DNS validation (recommended, enables auto-renew) or email validation
Certificates are Regional; CloudFront requires the certificate in us-east-1
Public certificates are free when used with integrated services; exportable public certificates are billed per certificate
Validity for public certificates follows CA/B Forum reductions (moving to shorter lifetimes)
services.pricingModel: Public certs for integrated services free; exportable public certificates per FQDN; AWS Private CA per CA per month plus per private certificate.

comparesWith.difference: KMS manages encryption keys; ACM manages X.509 certificates and their private keys for TLS.

recentLaunches.title: ACME protocol support for automated public TLS certificate issuance and renewal

interviewTips: Remember the us-east-1 requirement for CloudFront certificates and use DNS validation with Route 53 for zero-touch renewal

services.name: Amazon Detective
services.oneLiner: Builds a behavior graph from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, EKS audit logs and GuardDuty findings to speed security investigations.
whenToUse: Root-cause analysis and scoping of GuardDuty/Security Hub findings
Visualizing entity activity (IAM roles, IPs, instances) over up to a year of history
whenNotToUse: Primary detection (use GuardDuty) or long-term SIEM storage (Security Lake/third-party SIEM)
keyFacts: Requires GuardDuty enabled for at least 48 hours before enabling
Retains up to 1 year of aggregated behavior data; finding groups cluster related findings
Generative AI summaries of finding groups
services.pricingModel: Per GB of data ingested into the behavior graph (tiered); 30-day free trial.

comparesWith.difference: GuardDuty detects; Detective investigates.
Security Lake is a data lake for raw logs queried by your tools; Detective is a purpose-built investigation UI.

interviewTips: Place Detective in the incident response lifecycle after detection and before containment decisions

services.name: Amazon Security Lake
services.oneLiner: Centralizes AWS, SaaS, on-prem and custom security logs into an S3 data lake normalized to OCSF in Apache Iceberg/Parquet.
whenToUse: Long-term, cost-effective security log retention with a common schema across sources
Feeding multiple SIEM/analytics subscribers (Splunk, OpenSearch, Athena) without duplicating pipelines
whenNotToUse: Small environments that only need GuardDuty/Security Hub findings
keyFacts: Native sources: CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver logs, Security Hub findings, S3 data events, EKS audit logs, WAF logs, Lambda data events
Rollup Regions consolidate data; lifecycle and retention configured per Region
Subscribers get data access (S3/Lake Formation) or query access (Athena)
services.pricingModel: Per GB ingested and normalized (AWS sources) plus S3 storage and subscriber query costs.

comparesWith.difference: Security Hub manages and prioritizes findings; Security Lake stores normalized raw telemetry.
CloudTrail generates API logs; Security Lake centralizes and normalizes them with other sources.

interviewTips: Mention OCSF as the reason multiple tools can consume the same data

services.name: AWS Verified Access
services.oneLiner: Zero-trust, VPN-less access to corporate applications and resources, evaluating identity and device posture on every request.
whenToUse: Replacing client VPN for employee access to internal web apps (HTTP) and non-HTTP resources (TCP: SSH, RDP, databases)
Fine-grained access policies written in Cedar using IdP and device-management signals
whenNotToUse: Site-to-site network connectivity (use VPN/Direct Connect)
Public customer-facing apps (use CloudFront + WAF + Cognito)
keyFacts: Trust providers: IAM Identity Center or OIDC IdPs for users; CrowdStrike, Jamf, JumpCloud for device posture
Policies in Cedar at group and endpoint level; integrates with WAF for web endpoints
Logs every access attempt for audit (OCSF format supported)
services.pricingModel: Per application (endpoint) hour plus per GB processed; non-HTTP endpoints billed per connection-hour.

comparesWith.difference: VPN grants network-level access; Verified Access grants per-app access with continuous identity/device checks.

interviewTips: Tie Verified Access to zero-trust principles: no implicit network trust, per-request authorization

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.oneLiner: Serverless interactive SQL (Trino-based) and Apache Spark over data in S3 and federated sources, paying per data scanned or reserved capacity.
whenToUse: Ad-hoc queries on S3 data lakes (Parquet/ORC/Iceberg), logs (CloudTrail, ALB, VPC Flow) and CUR data
Federated queries to DynamoDB, RDS, Redshift, Snowflake etc. via managed connectors
whenNotToUse: High-concurrency, low-latency dashboards on hot data (Redshift or a serving store)
Large volumes of unpartitioned CSV/JSON scanned repeatedly (convert to columnar first)
keyFacts: SQL engine v3 (Trino); DML/time travel on Apache Iceberg tables; Glue Data Catalog as metastore
Default DML query timeout 30 minutes; 20+ concurrent DML queries per account by default (adjustable)
Cost control: partitioning, partition projection, compression, columnar formats, workgroup data-usage limits
Capacity Reservations now 1-minute granularity with 4 DPU minimum (Feb 2026); query result reuse caching
Managed federated connectors for 12 sources (Apr 2026) and Glue Data Catalog materialized views
services.pricingModel: Per TB of data scanned (10 MB minimum per query) or Provisioned Capacity per DPU-hour; Spark per DPU-hour; S3/Glue costs separate.

comparesWith.difference: Redshift is a provisioned/serverless warehouse tuned for heavy repeated BI; Athena is pay-per-query over S3.
EMR runs custom Spark/Hadoop jobs at scale with cluster control; Athena is serverless SQL.

recentLaunches.title: 1-minute Capacity Reservations and 4 DPU minimum
Managed connectors simplify federated queries

interviewTips: Explain how partitioning and Parquet reduce scanned bytes (and therefore cost) by orders of magnitude

services.name: AWS Glue

Central Hive-compatible metadata catalog for Athena, EMR, Redshift Spectrum and Lake Formation
Schema discovery with crawlers and data quality rules (DQDL)
whenNotToUse: Long-running, highly tuned Spark jobs where EMR (on EC2/EKS) is cheaper or more flexible

Glue 6.0 (Aug 2026): ~30% lower price and full Apache Iceberg v3 support

services.pricingModel: Per DPU-hour for jobs, crawlers, interactive sessions and Data Quality; Data Catalog storage/requests beyond free tier.

comparesWith.difference: EMR gives full cluster control and many frameworks; Glue is serverless Spark with a catalog.

recentLaunches.title: Glue Ray jobs move to maintenance (no new customers from Apr 30, 2026)
Glue 6.0 with 30% lower price and Apache Iceberg v3

services.name: Amazon EMR
services.oneLiner: Managed big-data platform for Spark, Hive, Presto/Trino, Flink and HBase on EC2, EKS or EMR Serverless.
whenToUse: Large-scale Spark/Hadoop processing needing custom configs, libraries or specific instance types
Cost-optimized batch with Spot task nodes and instance fleets
EMR Serverless for Spark/Hive jobs without cluster management
whenNotToUse: Simple SQL on S3 (Athena) or small ETL where Glue is simpler
keyFacts: Node types: primary (master), core (HDFS + tasks), task (compute only — ideal for Spot)

comparesWith.difference: Glue is serverless with less control; EMR offers any framework/version and cluster tuning.

services.name: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
services.oneLiner: Managed real-time data streaming with ordered shards, replay and multiple consumers; on-demand or provisioned capacity.
whenToUse: Real-time ingestion of clickstreams, logs, IoT and CDC events with multiple independent consumers
Ordered processing per partition key and replay within retention
whenNotToUse: Simple point-to-point queueing with per-message deletes (SQS)
Kafka-compatible ecosystems/protocols (MSK)
keyFacts: Per shard: 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s writes; 2 MB/s reads shared (or 2 MB/s per consumer with enhanced fan-out)
Max record size 10 MiB (configurable, default 1 MiB; raised Oct 2025); PutRecords request up to 10 MiB
Retention 24 hours default, extendable to 7 days or up to 365 days (long-term retention)
On-demand mode scales automatically (default up to 200 MB/s write per stream, higher on request); provisioned mode scales by shards
Ordering guaranteed within a shard via partition key; at-least-once delivery

services.name: Amazon Data Firehose
services.oneLiner: Fully managed streaming delivery (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) that buffers, transforms and loads data into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Iceberg tables, Splunk and HTTP endpoints.
whenToUse: Zero-admin loading of logs/events into S3 data lakes (with Parquet conversion and dynamic partitioning) or Apache Iceberg tables
Streaming into Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Snowflake or third-party HTTP destinations
whenNotToUse: Sub-second latency or custom consumers with replay (use Kinesis Data Streams/MSK)
keyFacts: Renamed from Kinesis Data Firehose to Amazon Data Firehose in Feb 2024
Buffering by size (1–128 MiB) and interval (0–900 s); near real-time, not real-time
Optional Lambda transformation, format conversion to Parquet/ORC, dynamic partitioning
Sources: Direct PUT, Kinesis Data Streams, MSK, CloudWatch Logs, VPC Flow Logs, IoT, WAF; max record 1,000 KiB
services.pricingModel: Per GB ingested (5 KB increments), plus format conversion, dynamic partitioning and VPC delivery charges.

comparesWith.difference: Data Streams stores data for replay and custom consumers; Firehose is delivery-only.

interviewTips: Use the renamed service name "Amazon Data Firehose" and explain the buffering trade-off between latency and file size

services.name: Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka)
services.oneLiner: Managed Apache Kafka with Standard and Express brokers, MSK Serverless and MSK Connect.
whenToUse: Kafka-native applications, Kafka Streams/Connect ecosystems, or migrating self-managed Kafka
High-throughput event streaming with long retention and consumer groups
whenNotToUse: Teams without Kafka expertise needing simple streaming (Kinesis) or queueing (SQS)
keyFacts: Express brokers: up to 3x more throughput per broker, up to 20x faster scaling and 90% faster recovery vs Standard; storage managed and pay-as-you-go

services.pricingModel: Provisioned: per broker-hour plus storage (Standard) or per GB written/stored (Express); Serverless: per cluster-hour, partition-hour and GB in/out; Connect per MCU-hour.

comparesWith.difference: Kinesis is serverless-first with shards; MSK exposes Kafka APIs and configs.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.oneLiner: Managed OpenSearch (and legacy Elasticsearch) for search, log analytics, observability and vector search, provisioned or Serverless.

whenNotToUse: Primary system of record or transactional database

Purpose-built log analytics engine with 4x better price-performance
OpenSearch 3.7 with up to 5.5x faster vector search

Row-level and column-level security; embedding for anonymous or registered users

Amazon Quick desktop app GA on macOS and Windows

services.name: AWS Lake Formation

AWS PrivateLink support for private VPC connectivity
Amazon OpenSearch integration
