Centralized logs with Logs Insights queries, metric filters and subscription filters to Kinesis/Firehose/Lambda
APM with Application Signals (OpenTelemetry), canaries with Synthetics, and cross-account observability
whenNotToUse: Complex full-text log search/analytics at large scale where OpenSearch fits better
keyFacts: Metric resolution: standard 1 minute, high-resolution down to 1 second; retention 15 months with roll-ups (1-min data 15 days, 5-min 63 days, 1-h 455 days)
Log retention configurable from 1 day to 10 years or never expire; Infrequent Access log class is cheaper
Alarms: metric, composite and anomaly detection; log query alarms directly from Logs Insights (Jul 2026)
Unified data management and analytics for ops, security and compliance data (Dec 2025); managed Prometheus collectors (Jul 2026)
Embedded Metric Format extracts metrics from structured logs
services.pricingModel: Per custom metric-month, per API request, per alarm, per dashboard, per GB logs ingested/stored/scanned, per canary run, Application Signals per GB/requests; generous free tier.

comparesWith.difference: X-Ray is distributed tracing (now OpenTelemetry-based via CloudWatch Application Signals); CloudWatch covers metrics, logs and alarms.
CloudTrail logs API activity; CloudWatch monitors resource/app health.
OpenSearch gives advanced search/dashboards; CloudWatch is the native default for metrics/logs.

recentLaunches.title: Unified data management and analytics for operations, security and compliance
HTTP-based log ingestion protocol for CloudWatch Logs
Alarms directly from log queries
Managed collectors for Prometheus metrics

interviewTips: Define SLIs/SLOs and alarm on symptoms (latency/error rates) rather than only causes (CPU)
Control log cost: retention policies, IA log class, sampling, and metric filters instead of storing everything

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.oneLiner: Declarative infrastructure as code (JSON/YAML) that provisions stacks of AWS resources with change sets, drift detection, StackSets and hooks.
whenToUse: Repeatable, reviewable infrastructure deployments with rollback on failure
Multi-account/multi-Region deployment via StackSets (with Organizations auto-deployment)
Proactive compliance with CloudFormation Hooks and Guard rules
whenNotToUse: Multi-cloud IaC standards (Terraform/OpenTofu/Pulumi) — though CDK can target CloudFormation
keyFacts: Template limits: 1 MB (via S3), 500 resources per stack, 200 parameters, 200 outputs; 2,000 stacks per account default
Change sets preview changes; stack policies and termination protection prevent accidental updates/deletes
DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy (Retain, Snapshot) protect stateful resources
Drift detection identifies out-of-band changes; resource import brings existing resources under management
Express mode (Jun 2026) speeds deployments up to 4x for fast iteration (e.g. AI agents)
services.pricingModel: No charge for AWS resource types; third-party/private resource types and hooks billed per handler operation.

comparesWith.difference: CDK lets you write IaC in TypeScript/Python/Java/etc. and synthesizes CloudFormation templates.
Service Catalog publishes approved CloudFormation/Terraform products for self-service.

recentLaunches.title: StackSets deployment ordering for auto-deployment mode
CloudFormation Express mode — up to 4x faster deployments

interviewTips: Explain nested stacks vs cross-stack references (exports) and the coupling trade-offs

services.name: AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)
services.oneLiner: Open-source IaC framework to define cloud infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Java, C# or Go using constructs, synthesized to CloudFormation.
whenToUse: Teams that prefer general-purpose languages, abstraction, testing and reuse (L2/L3 constructs, Construct Hub)
Application and infrastructure defined together in the same repo with CDK Pipelines
whenNotToUse: Organizations standardized on Terraform, or teams that want purely declarative templates
keyFacts: Construct levels: L1 (Cfn resources), L2 (curated with defaults), L3 (patterns)
cdk synth → CloudFormation template; cdk deploy uses change sets; cdk diff previews
Bootstrapping creates staging bucket/ECR repo and deployment roles per account/Region
CDK v2 is a single package (aws-cdk-lib); CDK Toolkit library allows programmatic deployments
services.pricingModel: Free and open source; pay for the resources deployed.

comparesWith.difference: CloudFormation is the deployment engine and template language; CDK generates templates from code.

interviewTips: Mention unit tests with assertions and aspects/cdk-nag for policy checks

services.name: AWS Systems Manager
services.oneLiner: Operations hub for EC2, on-prem and edge nodes: Session Manager, Run Command, Patch Manager, Parameter Store, Automation, State Manager and Inventory.
whenToUse: Keyless, audited shell access without bastions or open SSH ports (Session Manager)
Fleet patching, configuration and runbooks at scale (Patch Manager, State Manager, Automation)
Configuration/secrets storage (Parameter Store standard free up to 10,000 parameters)
whenNotToUse: New use of Change Manager, Incident Manager (closed to new customers Nov 7, 2025) or Application Manager (Jul 30, 2026)
keyFacts: Requires SSM Agent and an instance profile (or Default Host Management Configuration); private subnets need VPC endpoints (ssm, ssmmessages, ec2messages)
Parameter Store: standard 4 KB values (free), advanced 8 KB with policies (charged); SecureString uses KMS
Session Manager logs sessions to S3/CloudWatch; port forwarding for RDP/DB access
Unified node management console across accounts/Regions; hybrid activations for on-prem servers
services.pricingModel: Most core features free; charges for advanced parameters, higher-throughput Parameter Store API, advanced on-prem instances, Automation steps beyond free tier, OpsCenter items.

comparesWith.difference: Secrets Manager adds automatic rotation and cross-Region replication; Parameter Store is cheaper for config.
Config detects non-compliance; SSM Automation remediates it.

recentLaunches.title: Change Manager and Incident Manager move to maintenance (no new customers from Nov 7, 2025)

interviewTips: Replace bastion hosts with Session Manager for security and auditability

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.oneLiner: Automated best-practice checks across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence.
whenToUse: Quick account health review for idle resources, open security groups, missing MFA, quota usage
Organizational view of checks for Business/Enterprise Support customers
whenNotToUse: Deep rightsizing analysis (Compute Optimizer) or compliance frameworks (Security Hub CSPM)
keyFacts: Basic/Developer support: core security checks and service quota checks only; Business/Enterprise: full check set and API access
Priority recommendations curated by the account team for Enterprise Support
Integrates with EventBridge for automated responses
services.pricingModel: Included with AWS Support plans; the full check set requires Business, Enterprise On-Ramp or Enterprise Support.

comparesWith.difference: Compute Optimizer uses ML on utilization metrics for rightsizing; Trusted Advisor runs broad rule-based checks.
The WA Tool is a question-based workload review; Trusted Advisor inspects account resources automatically.

interviewTips: Mention the service quota checks when discussing scaling readiness before launches

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.oneLiner: Distributed tracing for request flows across services; X-Ray SDKs/Daemon entered maintenance Feb 25, 2026 in favor of OpenTelemetry (ADOT/CloudWatch agent).
whenToUse: Tracing latency and errors across Lambda, API Gateway, ECS/EKS and downstream calls via service maps
Existing X-Ray instrumentation (the backend still accepts traces)
whenNotToUse: New instrumentation with X-Ray SDKs — use OpenTelemetry (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry) and CloudWatch Application Signals
keyFacts: X-Ray SDKs and Daemon: maintenance from Feb 25, 2026, end of support Feb 25, 2027
Sampling rules control volume (default 1 request/s plus 5% of additional requests)
Traces retained 30 days; segments/subsegments with annotations (indexed) and metadata (not indexed)
Transaction Search in CloudWatch ingests spans for full-fidelity analysis
services.pricingModel: Per million traces recorded and per million traces retrieved/scanned (free tier of 100,000 recorded traces/month).

comparesWith.difference: CloudWatch Application Signals is the OpenTelemetry-based APM experience that now subsumes X-Ray views.

recentLaunches.title: X-Ray SDKs and Daemon enter maintenance mode (EOS Feb 25, 2027)

interviewTips: Show currency: recommend OpenTelemetry instrumentation for new services

services.name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
services.oneLiner: Free console tool to review workloads against the six Well-Architected pillars and lenses, track risks and improvement plans.
whenToUse: Structured architecture reviews with customers (a core SA activity) and milestone tracking
Applying lenses (Serverless, SaaS, Generative AI, Financial Services, Streaming Media, etc.) and custom org lenses
whenNotToUse: Automated resource-level checks (use Trusted Advisor, Config, Security Hub)
keyFacts: Pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability
Identifies high and medium risk issues (HRIs/MRIs); integrates Trusted Advisor data for workloads
Custom lenses and profiles; review templates; sharing across accounts
Updated Streaming Media Lens (Sep 2026)
services.pricingModel: No charge.

comparesWith.difference: Trusted Advisor is automated account checks; the WA Tool is a guided question-based review.

recentLaunches.title: Updated Well-Architected Streaming Media Lens

interviewTips: Be ready to name the six pillars and give one design principle and one anti-pattern per pillar

services.name: AWS Service Catalog
services.oneLiner: Curated portfolios of approved IaC products (CloudFormation or Terraform) that users can self-provision with governance constraints.
whenToUse: Self-service provisioning of approved architectures with launch constraints (no direct IAM needed)
Account vending (Control Tower Account Factory is built on it); sharing portfolios across the organization
whenNotToUse: Teams deploying their own IaC via CI/CD without a central catalog
New AppRegistry usage — Service Catalog AppRegistry is closed to new customers (Jul 30, 2026)
keyFacts: Constructs: portfolios, products (versions), constraints (launch, notification, template, tag update, StackSet)
Supports CloudFormation and Terraform (open source and Terraform Cloud) products
AppRegistry entered maintenance Jul 30, 2026
services.pricingModel: Per API call beyond the free tier (first 1,000 calls/month free).

comparesWith.difference: CloudFormation deploys templates; Service Catalog governs who can deploy which approved templates.
Control Tower Account Factory uses Service Catalog to vend new accounts.

interviewTips: Use launch constraints so end users can provision products without broad IAM permissions

services.name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS)
services.oneLiner: Continuous block-level replication of on-prem, other-cloud or EC2 servers into a low-cost staging area for recovery on EC2 in minutes (RPO seconds).
whenToUse: Pilot-light style DR for servers with RPO of seconds and RTO of minutes without paying for full standby compute
Cross-Region or cross-AZ DR for EC2 workloads; non-disruptive recovery drills
whenNotToUse: Managed databases with native replication (Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables, RDS cross-Region replicas)
One-time migrations (use Application Migration Service)
keyFacts: Continuous replication via agent to lightweight replication servers and EBS in a staging subnet; point-in-time recovery snapshots
Typical RPO seconds, RTO minutes; failback to on-prem or original Region supported
Recovery Plans (Aug 2026) orchestrate sequential multi-server launches with approvals and drill mode
Faster recovery for AWS-to-AWS workloads (up to 65% less time for Windows, Jul 2026); IPv6 support (Apr 2026)
services.pricingModel: Per replicating source server per hour, plus staging EBS, snapshots and replication servers; recovery instances billed at EC2 rates only when launched.

comparesWith.difference: MGN uses similar replication for one-time migration; DRS keeps servers continuously protected for DR.
AWS Backup gives periodic backups (RPO hours); DRS gives continuous replication (RPO seconds).

recentLaunches.title: IPv6 support for replication and control plane
Reduced recovery time for AWS-to-AWS workloads
Recovery Plans for orchestrated application recovery

interviewTips: Place DRS on the DR spectrum (backup/restore → pilot light → warm standby → multi-site) with its RPO/RTO and cost

services.name: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
services.oneLiner: Recovery orchestration and traffic control: zonal shift/autoshift, Region switch plans and highly reliable routing controls for multi-AZ and multi-Region apps.
whenToUse: Shifting traffic away from an impaired AZ for ALB/NLB/EKS/ASG resources (zonal shift, zonal autoshift)
Orchestrating multi-Region failover runbooks across accounts with Region switch plans (Aurora, DocumentDB, Route 53, EC2, ECS, etc.)
Data-plane-only, highly available failover switches (routing controls) independent of control planes
whenNotToUse: Single-AZ/single-Region workloads without redundant capacity to shift to
New use of readiness checks — closed to new customers since Apr 30, 2026
keyFacts: Zonal shift: temporary (up to 3 days, extendable) at no extra cost; zonal autoshift lets AWS shift automatically during AZ impairments, with practice runs
Routing controls run on a 5-Region cluster with highly available data-plane endpoints; safety rules prevent unsafe states
Region switch: plans with execution blocks, cross-account support, automatic execution reports to S3 (Dec 2025)
Formerly named Route 53 Application Recovery Controller
services.pricingModel: Zonal shift/autoshift free; routing control clusters billed per hour; Region switch billed per plan per month.

comparesWith.difference: Route 53 health-check failover is automatic DNS-based; ARC routing controls give deliberate, highly reliable manual control.
Resilience Hub assesses and tracks resilience posture; ARC executes recovery actions.
FIS injects failures (and can trigger zonal autoshift recovery actions) to test ARC-based recovery.

recentLaunches.title: ARC Region switch — multi-Region application recovery orchestration
Region switch adds execution reports, DocumentDB global cluster blocks and GovCloud support
Readiness check moves to maintenance

interviewTips: Explain static stability and why failover should rely on data-plane operations, not control-plane API calls during an event

services.name: AWS Resilience Hub
services.oneLiner: Defines resilience policies (RTO/RPO, SLOs) and assesses applications against them with AI-powered failure-mode analysis, dependency discovery and org-wide reporting.
whenToUse: Setting and tracking resilience targets across an application portfolio
Discovering hidden dependencies and failure modes before incidents; generating recommended alarms, SOPs and FIS experiments
whenNotToUse: Executing failover (ARC/DRS) or injecting faults (FIS) — Resilience Hub assesses and recommends
keyFacts: Next generation (May 28, 2026): modular policies, generative-AI failure mode analysis, DNS-log dependency discovery, user-journey application modeling
Organization-wide view from a delegated administrator account
Integrates with FIS, CloudWatch, SSM and Trusted Advisor-style recommendations
services.pricingModel: Per service assessed per month (includes two failure-mode assessments), with optional automated dependency assessment; free trial.

comparesWith.difference: The WA Tool is a questionnaire-based review; Resilience Hub analyzes deployed resources against policies.
FIS runs experiments; Resilience Hub recommends and tracks them.

recentLaunches.title: Next-generation Resilience Hub with generative AI-based assessments

interviewTips: Connect business RTO/RPO to architecture choices and show how you would continuously validate them

services.name: AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS)
services.oneLiner: Managed chaos engineering: run controlled fault-injection experiments (instance stops, latency, API errors, AZ power loss, Region connectivity) with stop conditions.
whenToUse: Validating that multi-AZ/multi-Region designs, alarms and runbooks actually work (game days)
Testing specific failures: EC2/ECS/EKS task termination, network disruption, Lambda faults, RDS/Aurora failover, DynamoDB MRSC Region failure, Direct Connect BGP failover
whenNotToUse: Production experiments without observability and CloudWatch alarm stop conditions in place
keyFacts: Experiment templates define actions, targets (by tags/filters) and stop conditions (CloudWatch alarms)
Scenario library: AZ power interruption, cross-Region connectivity, AZ application slowdown and cross-AZ traffic slowdown (Nov 2025)
Recovery action can trigger ARC zonal autoshift within the same experiment; multi-account experiments supported
services.pricingModel: Per action-minute of experiment run time (plus per-account charges for multi-account experiments).

comparesWith.difference: Resilience Hub assesses posture and recommends experiments; FIS executes them.
ARC performs recovery (zonal shift/Region switch); FIS simulates the failure that should trigger it.

recentLaunches.title: New scenarios for partial failures (AZ application slowdown, cross-AZ traffic slowdown)
Direct Connect BGP failover resilience testing
DynamoDB MRSC global tables resiliency testing

interviewTips: Describe a game day: hypothesis, steady-state metrics, blast radius, stop conditions, and learning review

services.name: AWS CodePipeline
services.oneLiner: Managed continuous delivery service that models release stages (source, build, test, deploy, approval) with triggers and variables.
whenToUse: AWS-native CI/CD for deploying to CloudFormation, ECS, Elastic Beanstalk, S3, CodeDeploy targets and Lambda
Cross-account deployment pipelines in multi-account landing zones
whenNotToUse: Teams already standardized on GitHub Actions/GitLab CI with OIDC federation to AWS
keyFacts: V2 pipeline type: Git triggers (branch/tag/file path filters), pipeline-level variables, parallel/queued/superseded execution modes
Stage-level conditions and automatic rollback on failure
Source actions: GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket via CodeConnections, S3, ECR, CodeCommit
Artifacts stored in S3 (encrypted with KMS); cross-account actions via assumed roles
services.pricingModel: V1: per active pipeline per month; V2: per action execution minute (with free tier).

comparesWith.difference: CodeBuild runs build/test jobs; CodePipeline orchestrates the overall release flow.

interviewTips: Design a multi-account pipeline (tooling account → dev → staging → prod) with manual approval and automated rollback

services.name: AWS CodeBuild
services.oneLiner: Fully managed build service that compiles, tests and packages code in ephemeral containers or reserved fleets.
whenToUse: Scalable CI builds without managing build servers; Docker image builds pushed to ECR
Managed runners for GitHub Actions, GitLab and Buildkite; reserved capacity fleets for faster starts (incl. macOS, GPU)
whenNotToUse: Long-running services — builds max out at 36 hours (default 60 minutes timeout)
keyFacts: buildspec.yml phases: install, pre_build, build, post_build; artifacts and reports
Compute: on-demand (EC2 or Lambda compute), reserved capacity fleets; Linux, Windows, Arm, macOS, GPU
Build timeout 5 minutes–36 hours; local and S3 caching; VPC support for private resources
Batch builds (build graphs, matrices)
services.pricingModel: Per build minute by compute type (Lambda compute per second), or per reserved fleet instance-minute; free tier minutes monthly.

comparesWith.difference: CodePipeline orchestrates; CodeBuild executes build/test steps.
CodeBuild builds container images; ECR stores them.

interviewTips: Mention secret handling (Secrets Manager/Parameter Store in buildspec env) and least-privilege service roles

services.name: AWS Migration Hub (closed to new customers — use AWS Transform)
services.oneLiner: Migration tracking and planning service (Strategy Recommendations, Orchestrator, Journeys) — closed to new customers since Nov 7, 2025; AWS Transform is the successor.
whenToUse: Existing customers completing in-flight migration projects tracked in Migration Hub
Existing customers reviewing historical migration status and data before moving to AWS Transform (no data migration required)
whenNotToUse: Any new migration program — use AWS Transform (agentic assessment, VMware/mainframe/.NET/Windows modernization and migration planning)
keyFacts: Maintenance since Nov 7, 2025 (announced Oct 7, 2025); existing customers continue with security updates
Application Discovery Service also moved to maintenance (Oct/Nov 2025)
AWS Transform (launched May 2025) includes equivalent capabilities: strategy recommendations, EC2 recommendations, journeys, orchestration; no data migration required
services.pricingModel: No charge for Migration Hub itself (existing customers); AWS Transform has free agent capabilities with usage limits.

comparesWith.difference: MGN performs the rehost replication/cutover; Migration Hub only tracked progress.
DMS migrates databases; Migration Hub tracked the overall portfolio.
AWS Transform is the successor, adding agentic assessment, wave planning and modernization.

recentLaunches.title: Migration Hub moves to maintenance (no new customers from Nov 7, 2025); successor AWS Transform

interviewTips: For migration questions, cover the 7 Rs and name AWS Transform for assessment/planning plus MGN/DMS/DataSync for execution

services.name: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)
services.oneLiner: Primary rehost (lift-and-shift) service: continuous block-level replication of physical, VMware, Hyper-V and cloud servers to EC2 with test and cutover launches.
whenToUse: Large-scale server migrations with minimal downtime (cutover in minutes)
Cross-Region/cross-AZ EC2 migrations; replatforming actions via post-launch modernization
whenNotToUse: Database engine changes or managed DB targets (use DMS)
Ongoing DR replication (use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, which shares the technology)
keyFacts: Replication agent on source; staging area subnet with low-cost replication servers and EBS
Non-disruptive test launches before cutover; launch templates control target instance settings
Free for 90 days (2,160 hours) per server; post-launch actions (SSM) for modernization
IPv6/dual-stack service endpoints (Dec 2025)
services.pricingModel: Free for 2,160 hours per source server; afterwards per server-hour; you pay for staging EC2/EBS and target resources.

comparesWith.difference: DMS migrates data at the database level (homogeneous/heterogeneous); MGN copies whole servers.
Migration Hub is closed to new customers; use AWS Transform for planning and MGN for execution.

recentLaunches.title: IPv6 support via dual-stack service endpoints

interviewTips: Explain a wave-based migration: discovery → test launch → cutover window → decommission, with rollback plan

services.name: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
services.oneLiner: Migrates and continuously replicates databases (full load + CDC) between homogeneous or heterogeneous engines, with Schema Conversion and DMS Serverless.
whenToUse: Near-zero-downtime database migrations using change data capture
Heterogeneous moves (Oracle/SQL Server → Aurora PostgreSQL) with DMS Schema Conversion
Ongoing replication to data lakes/warehouses (S3, Redshift, Kinesis)
whenNotToUse: Where native tools are faster/simpler for homogeneous moves (e.g. pg_dump, native replication, Aurora read-replica promotion)
keyFacts: Replication instances (sized, Multi-AZ option) or DMS Serverless (auto-scaling capacity units)
Task types: full load, full load + CDC, CDC only; validation compares source and target
Schema Conversion (in DMS) and the standalone AWS SCT convert schema and code objects
DMS Fleet Advisor reached end of support (2025)
services.pricingModel: Per replication instance-hour (or Serverless DCU-hour) plus storage; Schema Conversion free; data transfer into AWS free.

comparesWith.difference: MGN migrates entire servers; DMS migrates database contents to a new engine/instance.
DataSync copies files/objects; DMS replicates database rows with CDC.

interviewTips: Describe the cutover: full load, CDC catch-up, validation, stop writes, final sync, switch connection strings

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.oneLiner: Online data transfer service that moves files and objects between on-prem storage, other clouds and AWS storage with encryption and integrity checks.
whenToUse: Bulk and scheduled transfers from NFS/SMB/HDFS/object storage to S3, EFS or FSx
Migrating from other clouds (Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage) — agentless in Enhanced mode for some sources
The recommended online alternative to Snowball Edge for new customers
whenNotToUse: Low-latency ongoing hybrid file access (Storage Gateway)
Database replication (DMS)
keyFacts: Agent (VM) for on-prem sources; Enhanced mode scales transfers with no file count limits for S3 and (Jul 2026) EFS/FSx for Lustre
Up to 10 Gbps per agent/task in Basic mode; bandwidth throttling and scheduling; incremental transfers
Data verification and TLS encryption in transit; transfers over internet, VPN or Direct Connect
DataSync Discovery reached end of support (2025)
services.pricingModel: Per GB transferred (Enhanced mode adds per-task execution fees); plus storage and data transfer charges.

comparesWith.difference: Snowball Edge is offline physical transfer and closed to new customers since Nov 7, 2025; DataSync is online.
Transfer Family provides SFTP/FTPS/AS2 endpoints for partners; DataSync is bulk movement between storage systems.

recentLaunches.title: Enhanced mode supports Amazon EFS and FSx for Lustre

interviewTips: Estimate transfer time from bandwidth (e.g. 100 TB over 1 Gbps ≈ 10 days at 100% utilization) to decide online vs offline

services.name: AWS Snow Family (Snowball Edge closed to new customers)
services.oneLiner: Rugged devices for offline data transfer and disconnected edge compute — Snowball Edge devices are only available to existing customers since Nov 7, 2025; Snowmobile and Snowcone are retired.
whenToUse: Existing customers moving large datasets where network transfer is impractical
Existing customers running disconnected/tactical edge compute (existing customers can still order devices)
whenNotToUse: New customers — use DataSync (online), AWS Data Transfer Terminal (physical drop-off), partner solutions, or Outposts for edge compute
keyFacts: Snowball Edge Storage Optimized and Compute Optimized entered maintenance (announced Oct 7, 2025; closed to new customers Nov 7, 2025)
Existing customers can still order devices after that date
Data encrypted with 256-bit keys managed by KMS; tamper-evident enclosure and TPM; import to S3
services.pricingModel: Per-job service fee including days on site, plus extra days and data transfer out of AWS (import to S3 free).

comparesWith.difference: DataSync transfers online and is recommended for new customers.
Outposts is the recommended connected edge compute alternative.

recentLaunches.title: Snowball Edge moves to maintenance (existing customers only from Nov 7, 2025)

interviewTips: Show currency: for a "move 500 TB with limited bandwidth" question, mention Snowball is closed to new customers and propose Direct Connect + DataSync or Data Transfer Terminal

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.oneLiner: Fully managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 endpoints (plus web apps and connectors) backed by S3 or EFS.
whenToUse: B2B file exchange with partners who require SFTP/AS2 without running file servers
Managed workflows to process files on upload; SFTP connectors to push/pull from external servers
whenNotToUse: Internal bulk migrations (DataSync) or application object access (S3 APIs)
keyFacts: Identity providers: service-managed (SSH keys), AWS Directory Service, or custom IdP via Lambda/API Gateway
Endpoint types: public, VPC (internal or internet-facing with Elastic IPs for allow-listing)
Managed workflows for post-upload processing (copy, tag, decrypt, custom Lambda)
services.pricingModel: Per protocol endpoint-hour plus per GB uploaded/downloaded; connectors and web apps billed separately.

comparesWith.difference: DataSync moves data between storage systems; Transfer Family serves protocol endpoints for external users.

recentLaunches.title: Available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand)

interviewTips: Use VPC endpoint type with Elastic IPs when partners need static IPs to allow-list

services.name: AWS Transform
services.oneLiner: Agentic AI service (launched May 2025) for migration and modernization: VMware migration planning, mainframe, .NET/Windows full-stack, custom code transformations and continuous modernization.
whenToUse: Assessing portfolios and building migration business cases/TCO (successor to Migration Hub capabilities)
Modernizing .NET Framework to cross-platform .NET, mainframe COBOL, VMware to EC2 (incl. network conversion), and Java/Python upgrades via Transform Custom
Reducing tech debt continuously across repositories
whenNotToUse: Executing server replication/cutover itself (MGN) or database replication (DMS) — Transform plans and orchestrates, these tools execute
keyFacts: Generally available May 2025; replaced Migration Hub (closed to new customers Nov 7, 2025) and Q Developer transformation features
Re:Invent 2025: Transform Custom (organization-specific code transformations) and full-stack Windows modernization; mainframe reimagine and automated testing
Available in Kiro and VS Code (Apr 2026); continuous modernization GA (Jul 2026); .NET CLI with 50,000 free agent minutes/month (Sep 2026)
Human-in-the-loop: agents propose plans and changes that teams review and approve
services.pricingModel: Core migration/modernization agent capabilities offered at no charge within usage limits; some capabilities (e.g. Transform Custom) are billed by agent usage.

comparesWith.difference: Migration Hub is closed to new customers; Transform provides its planning capabilities plus AI-driven modernization.
MGN performs rehost replication; Transform generates wave plans and orchestrates migrations using MGN.
DMS moves database data; Transform focuses on code and application modernization/planning.

recentLaunches.title: AWS Transform Custom — AI-powered code modernization for enterprise tech debt
Assessment capabilities for migration business cases and TCO
Continuous modernization generally available
.NET modernization CLI with 50,000 free agent minutes per month

interviewTips: Show currency in migration answers: AWS Transform for assessment/planning/modernization, then MGN, DMS and DataSync for execution

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer
services.oneLiner: Visualizes, filters and forecasts AWS cost and usage, with Savings Plans/RI coverage and utilization reports and recommendations.
whenToUse: Exploring spend by service, account, tag, Region; 12-month forecasts
Savings Plans/RI purchase recommendations and coverage tracking
whenNotToUse: Line-item analytics at scale (use CUR 2.0 / Data Exports with Athena or QuickSight/Quick dashboards)
keyFacts: Up to 13 months of history (38 months at monthly granularity with multi-year data enabled) and 12-month forecasts
Hourly and resource-level granularity available (opt-in, charged)
Cost allocation tags must be activated to appear; Cost Categories group costs by rules
Cost Anomaly Detection uses ML to alert on unusual spend
services.pricingModel: Console use free; API requests per request; hourly/resource-level data charged per usage record.

comparesWith.difference: Budgets alerts/acts on thresholds; Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts.
Compute Optimizer recommends rightsizing; Cost Explorer shows spend and purchase recommendations.

recentLaunches.title: CUR 2.0 integration with Athena and Redshift
AWS FinOps Agent (preview) answers cost questions and investigates anomalies

interviewTips: Present a FinOps loop: tagging strategy → visibility (Cost Explorer/CUR) → optimization (rightsizing, Savings Plans) → governance (Budgets, SCPs)

services.name: AWS Budgets
services.oneLiner: Sets custom cost, usage, Savings Plans and RI budgets with alerts and automated budget actions.
whenToUse: Alerting teams when actual or forecasted spend exceeds thresholds
Guardrails: budget actions apply IAM/SCP policies or stop EC2/RDS instances when exceeded
whenNotToUse: Hard spending caps — AWS has no universal hard cap; budgets alert/act after data refresh (up to ~3 times daily)
keyFacts: Budget types: cost, usage, Savings Plans utilization/coverage, RI utilization/coverage
Notifications via email, SNS and Chatbot/Amazon Q in chat apps
Budget actions can require approval before applying

services.name: Savings Plans
services.oneLiner: Flexible pricing model offering discounts for a 1- or 3-year $/hour commitment — Compute, EC2 Instance, SageMaker AI and (since Dec 2025) Database Savings Plans.
whenToUse: Covering steady-state baseline usage across EC2, Fargate, Lambda (Compute SP) or specific instance families (EC2 Instance SP)
Database spend across Aurora, RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, DocumentDB, Neptune, Keyspaces, Timestream, DMS, OpenSearch (Database SP)
whenNotToUse: Spiky or short-lived usage (use On-Demand/Spot) or when capacity reservation is required (Savings Plans do not reserve capacity)
keyFacts: Compute Savings Plans: up to 66% off, apply across instance family, size, OS, tenancy, Region, and to Fargate and Lambda
EC2 Instance Savings Plans: up to 72% off for a chosen instance family in a Region
Database Savings Plans (Dec 2, 2025): 1-year term; up to 35% for serverless, 20% provisioned, 18%/12% for DynamoDB/Keyspaces on-demand/provisioned; apply across Regions and engines
Payment options: all upfront, partial upfront, no upfront; commitments apply to the lowest-priced usage first
Do not reserve capacity — pair with On-Demand Capacity Reservations when needed
